exposure: Duration of breastfeeding (<6 months vs. ≥6 months)
outcome: Motor development outcomes at 10, 14, and 17 years of age
cohort: 2868 children from the Western Australian Pregnancy (Raine) Study
finding: Breastfeeding for 6 months or more was positively associated with improved motor development outcomes at 10, 14, and 17 years of age, independent of sociodemographic factors.
mod_finding: Breastfeeding for 6 months or more was positively associated with improved motor development outcomes at 10, 14, and 17 years of age, even when adjusted for mode of delivery.
